decisions.text: Scope is at the program level; not at tenant-level.
decisions.source: PCE PRD §2 Key Product Decisions #1

decisions.text: For Clinical Course, preceptor and site evaluations stay within learning activities — CE for clinical courses focuses only on course content/structure, the course coordinator (DCE), and Course Instructor.
decisions.source: PCE PRD §2 Key Product Decisions #3

decisions.text: Survey responses are anonymous: no student identifier is attached to the submitted response.
decisions.source: PCE PRD §4.3 Step 3 — Response Collection

decisions.text: Minimum response threshold is 5 — results for any course suppressed until minimum 5 responses received.
decisions.source: PCE PRD §9 Non-Functional Requirements

decisions.text: 1–5 Likert scale enforced as standard across all evaluations. Not a configurable option at faculty or program level.
decisions.source: PCE PRD §9 Non-Functional Requirements

decisions.text: Evaluation data retained for minimum 7 years to support longitudinal accreditation evidence.
decisions.source: PCE PRD §9 Non-Functional Requirements

decisions.text: The overall approach is to re-design Surveys in such a way that Course Evaluation and Survey can co-exist.
decisions.source: PCE PRD §2 Key Product Decisions #4

decisions.text: Three new constructs introduced to enable CE: Survey type (mandatory — Course evaluations or General surveys), Course type (optional — Didactic or Clinical), and Subject (assigned to each section).
decisions.source: PCE PRD §2 Key Product Decisions #5

decisions.text: We will just track submission and not the responses — survey responses are untraceable to individual students; no IP address, device ID, or response timing metadata exposed.
decisions.source: PCE PRD §9 Non-Functional Requirements — Anonymity/Privacy

decisions.text: FERPA does not apply to student-to-faculty course feedback — student feedback is voluntary and not classified as academic data (grades, scores, recordings). Faculty will not know the names of the students who submitted feedback. Anonymity is a design principle, not a FERPA requirement in this context.
decisions.source: Course evaluation and survey design — base entities, template workflow, and ETAs transcript — May 19, 2026

decisions.text: Template 'subjects' are populated from the program's Prism course-level role associations — the same lookup used by course role configuration. No separate subject list is maintained in PCE. If the program adds a new role, it flows through Prism-based configuration and auto-appears in PCE subject selection.
decisions.source: Post-course evaluation template — workflow, role-based access, and distribution setup with Monel transcript — May 19, 2026

decisions.text: A template section for a given subject will not render to the student if that subject (role) does not exist in the course offering. The same template can be used across all courses — sections appear or disappear based on the course's role configuration. This eliminates the need for separate templates per course type.
decisions.source: Post-course evaluation template — workflow, role-based access, and distribution setup with Monel transcript — May 19, 2026

decisions.text: PCE distribution must always be tied to a course — no distribution without course association. This is the key differentiator from general surveys. Faculty who want to push a survey without a course association must use the general survey tool.
decisions.source: Post-course evaluation template — workflow, role-based access, and distribution setup with Monel transcript — May 19, 2026

decisions.text: Phase 1 will not include predefined out-of-the-box templates. Users start with an empty template. Three creation paths: import an existing evaluation document (PDF/Word) via AI parsing, build manually question by question, or (future) pick from question bank. No vendor-provided starter templates.
decisions.source: Post-course evaluation template — workflow, role-based access, and distribution setup with Monel transcript — May 19, 2026

decisions.text: Distribution filters for course selection: term and academic year are required; cohort is optional and used by lockstep programs. These three filters together identify the course offerings to distribute to. For standalone (non-Prism) users, a quick-entry path for course name, number, term, and academic year must be provided.
decisions.source: Post-course evaluation template — workflow, role-based access, and distribution setup with Monel transcript — May 19, 2026

decisions.text: If a template has a course type (Didactic or Clinical) assigned, it auto-assigns to matching course offerings during distribution. If no course type is set in the template, manual course-type assignment is required per course during distribution setup.
decisions.source: Post-course evaluation template — workflow, role-based access, and distribution setup with Monel transcript — May 19, 2026

decisions.text: Guest lecturer evaluation is out of scope for PCE phase 1. It remains student-initiated and is handled via the general survey tool. Course coordinators initiating guest lecturer feedback can use PCE in a future phase once reliable event-based distribution is supported.
decisions.source: Post-course evaluation template — workflow, role-based access, and distribution setup with Monel transcript — May 19, 2026

decisions.text: Exam download capability is in scope for phase 1 — students must be able to download the exam to their local device within a coordinator-defined download window before the exam. Taking the exam must not require active Internet once downloaded. An explicit, actionable download prompt must be shown to students (not automatic background download).
decisions.source: Assessment creation workflows and question bank design transcript — May 19, 2026; confirmed in Assessment PRD — accessibility standards, offline exam download, and parity with ExamSoft transcript — May 21, 2026

decisions.text: The question bank exists at the base course level, not the course offering level. All offerings of the same base course share one question bank. Questions added during assessment creation or directly in the bank always save at the base course level — never at the offering level.
decisions.source: Assessment creation workflows and question bank design transcript — May 19, 2026

decisions.text: Question-level review and approval workflow is out of scope for at least 1 year minimum. Assessment-level review is in scope for phase 1. The review status checkbox currently shown in the question bank table must be removed.
decisions.source: Question bank design — move/copy options, design system alignment, and setup entities transcript — May 20, 2026

decisions.text: Phase 1 UI does not allow creating assessments outside a course context. All assessments must be created within a course. The backend must be architected to accommodate standalone assessments in the future, but no frontend capability will be built in phase 1.
decisions.source: Assessment creation workflows and question bank design transcript — May 19, 2026

decisions.text: Three roles for exam management: Admin (institution-wide superuser), Course Coordinator (superuser for their course — creates assessments, manages sections, views results), and Collaborator (flexible contributor — can add/edit questions in a course they are assigned to). The Collaborator role does not grant access to student results.
decisions.source: Assessment creation workflows and question bank design transcript — May 19, 2026

decisions.text: Review function is entirely separate from results access. A reviewer can give feedback on assessment questions before publishing but cannot view student scores or performance data. Only Admin and Course Coordinator (Director) roles can view student results. A reviewer's status per assessment is tracked independently.
decisions.source: Assessment creation workflows and question bank design transcript — May 19, 2026

decisions.text: Assignment assessment type is deprioritized for phase 1. Faculty use LMS (e.g., Canvas) for assignments and import scores there. Exam and Quiz are the primary supported assessment types. Assignment can be added to the backend, but no UI capability in phase 1.
decisions.source: Assessment creation workflows and question bank design transcript — May 19, 2026

decisions.text: AI tagging runs in the background for all questions. When manual tagging exists, it takes precedence over AI-generated tags. Both are visible — AI tags shown with an AI indicator, manual tags shown prominently. The system always maintains AI tags but defers to human judgment when there is a conflict.
decisions.source: Assessment creation workflows and question bank design transcript — May 19, 2026

decisions.text: Question rationale (explanation of the correct answer) is stored at the question bank level — never at the assessment level. It is editable within the assessment creation workflow, but all edits save back to the source question in the question bank. If rationale is missing, the assessment review screen must flag it.
decisions.source: Assessment creation workflows and question bank design transcript — May 19, 2026

decisions.text: Option position randomization within a question (locking individual option positions) is an ExamSoft parity feature and must be included in assessment setup configuration for phase 1. This is separate from question-level randomization (already captured) and section-level randomization.
decisions.source: Assessment creation workflows and question bank design transcript — May 19, 2026

decisions.text: Assessment creation supports exactly 4 methods: (1) Copy existing assessment — the most common use case (faculty recycle 5–15% of questions from previous exams); (2) AI prompt-based generation — faculty describe the assessment in natural language and AI selects questions from the bank; (3) Import PDF/document — AI parses an existing exam paper and creates the assessment; (4) Manual selection from question bank. No matter which method is used, the final review and publish steps are identical.
decisions.source: Assessment creation workflows and question bank design transcript — May 19, 2026; confirmed in Assessment question design — AI features, scoring, and workflow transcript — May 22, 2026

decisions.text: Phase 1 accessibility targets for the exam-taking experience: 200% magnification, text-to-speech (pending ExamSoft parity check), dyslexic font support, and high contrast color ratios. Accessibility compliance is acceptable to defer for the January launch but must reach parity with ExamSoft by phase 2 at latest.
decisions.source: Assessment PRD — accessibility standards, offline exam download, and parity with ExamSoft transcript — May 21, 2026

decisions.text: Point-by-serial score in the question bank table displays as plain text, not a bar chart. Aarti and Vishaka reviewed and rejected the bar concept.
decisions.source: Question bank design — move/copy options, design system alignment, and setup entities transcript — May 20, 2026

decisions.text: FAAS UI will be used as-is for question creation in the PCE template builder. The trade-off is user experience — FAAS UI follows the old design system while CE is built on the new design system.
decisions.source: PCE PRD §12 Dependencies and Risks — FAAS UI

decisions.text: Three entry points for CE results viewing: (1) by term — shows all courses in the term with per-term and per-course stats; (2) by faculty — shows all courses a faculty member has taught with per-faculty aggregated stats; (3) by course — shows all historical offerings of a course with per-course aggregated stats. The final 'evaluation card' (single course-offering result view) is identical regardless of which entry point is used.
decisions.source: Course and faculty evaluation setup — directories, templates, and term workflow transcript — Jun 10, 2026

decisions.text: Directory pages (student, faculty, course master list, course offering) within the CE module are VIEW-ONLY. They pull data from Prism base. No student/faculty/course management workflows are built inside CE. When a user needs to perform a data-management action (e.g., register a student to a course, add faculty to a course), they are deep-linked to the appropriate Prism page in a new tab. The underlying data resides only in Prism — CE never duplicates it.
decisions.source: Course and faculty evaluation setup — directories, templates, and term workflow transcript — Jun 10, 2026

decisions.text: Students do not get a login, profile creation, or invitation for course evaluations. Distribution is email-only: student email addresses are used to send an initial notification and reminders with a direct link. Students click the link to access and fill the evaluation. No student-facing authentication or account setup is required for CE participation.
decisions.source: Course and faculty evaluation setup — directories, templates, and term workflow transcript — Jun 10, 2026

decisions.text: Two reusable email templates exist in the CE setup: (1) initial notification sent when a survey opens, and (2) a reminder email template (dynamic — same template reused for all reminder cycles). The default reminder schedule is anchored on term end date (e.g., 15 days before term end). No separate template per reminder cycle is needed.
decisions.source: Course and faculty evaluation setup — directories, templates, and term workflow transcript — Jun 10, 2026

decisions.text: Academic year and term configuration — with start and end dates for each term — is a mandatory prerequisite for CE distribution automation. Without dates, the system cannot calculate when to open evaluations, send reminders, or close surveys. The CE setup section must require this configuration before a term can be enabled for CE. Terms with missing dates are excluded from the term-enablement workflow.
decisions.source: Course and faculty evaluation setup — directories, templates, and term workflow transcript — Jun 10, 2026; confirmed in India discussion — Weekly Product Sync | New Initiatives (Prism) transcript — Jun 10, 2026

decisions.text: The CE dashboard groups evaluations by term (not 'project'). Term is the primary organizing concept throughout the CE module — the landing page, dashboard, distribution flow, and analytics all anchor on the current term. Each term group shows its associated course offerings with KPIs and completion stats.
decisions.source: India discussion — Weekly Product Sync | New Initiatives (Prism) transcript — Jun 10, 2026

decisions.text: Longitudinal analytics requires two dedicated sidebar entry points: (1) Faculty — a faculty directory with leaderboard showing top/bottom performing faculty, search, and a detail view with spider graph (per-section scores), trend chart (historical rating), peer comparison, and per-course breakdown; (2) Course — a course directory showing all historical offerings of each course, with aggregated performance stats and click-through to individual offering results. These two pages are the key differentiators of PCE from a general survey tool.
decisions.source: India discussion — Weekly Product Sync | New Initiatives (Prism) transcript — Jun 10, 2026

decisions.text: Template sections have three categories: (1) Course content — questions about the course itself; (2) Faculty/roles — questions for faculty, with a multi-select of which program-level faculty roles from Prism this section applies to (all selected roles share the same questions in that section); (3) General — a catch-all section for questions not tied to a specific person or the course content. Multiple sections of each category can be added. The subject/role lookup is powered by program-level faculty role associations in Prism.
decisions.source: India discussion — Weekly Product Sync | New Initiatives (Prism) transcript — Jun 10, 2026

decisions.text: Faculty evaluation results must not be visible to other faculty. Faculty members should not be able to see each other's scores. This is an explicit design requirement for the CE module, addressing a known limitation of the current Prism product where all faculty can view each other's course evaluation data.
decisions.source: India discussion — Weekly Product Sync | New Initiatives (Prism) transcript — Jun 10, 2026

decisions.text: Template creation: 'Build new' has two sub-options — (a) manually add sections or (b) import from a PDF or Word document (AI parses and creates a draft template). The document import option is presented at the top-level template creation screen, not buried per section. No predefined vendor-provided starter templates are included in phase 1. The 'pick from question bank' path remains a future capability. Note: whether 'Copy existing template' is a supported path is unresolved — see DECISION CONFLICT in docs/watch/flags/pce.md dated 2026-06-09.
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jun 9, 2026

decisions.text: When adding sections to a template (Build new path): all desired sections/roles can be multi-selected in one action — no need to add one section at a time. Section descriptions are removed; only role/subject labels are shown. There is no per-section PDF import option (document import is top-level only). After choosing 'Build new', the user goes directly into the section-editing interface without additional intermediate option screens.
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jun 9, 2026

decisions.text: PCE distribution channel is Exact Prism only — no anonymous public link for course evaluations. The anonymous link option remains in the general survey tool only. Each student is permitted to submit only once per course evaluation, enforced by the backend using the Prism student roster for that course offering.
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jun 9, 2026

decisions.text: Anonymous response is a non-configurable default in CE — not an option the admin chooses. The distribution UI communicates 'responses are anonymous' as a statement to the admin, not as a toggle or question. The visibility/privacy toggle (private vs. share with program) shown in the general survey tool is removed from the CE distribution flow.
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jun 9, 2026

decisions.text: Comment moderation is a stretch goal for phase 1. If comment moderation is excluded: the results release date field becomes mandatory (not optional) in the distribution setup — the system uses this date to automatically distribute results to stakeholders. If no date is provided, the admin must manually share results; the UI must communicate this explicitly. Results must not be released to faculty before they have submitted final grades — the system cannot enforce this but must include a messaging reminder (soft, not a hard block).
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jun 9, 2026

decisions.text: Bulk distribution supports two levels of date override: (1) parent (term group) level — date changes cascade to all course instances in the same term distribution; (2) individual course instance level — override for a specific course without affecting others. Both granularities must be supported. The parent-level override is the primary workflow for extending survey windows across an entire term.
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jun 9, 2026

decisions.text: The Report Access step is removed from the CE distribution wizard in phase 1. Role-based access (program director and above) controls who can view all survey results — no per-survey access configuration is needed. If an admin wants to share specific evaluation data (e.g., a TA's results with a coordinator), they can manually download and email it. Phase 1 must remain simple: no custom report access rules per survey distribution. This resolves the PRD §4 vs. §13c.2 conflict flagged on 2026-06-09.
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jun 9, 2026

decisions.text: The general survey (programmatic survey) module UI, workflow, and backend are unchanged in this phase. Only the navigation entry point changes — CE and General Surveys are accessible as separate sidebar tabs within the same top-level module. No functional changes to the existing general survey workflow without a strong rationale and explicit approval, as users have already learned the current system and changing it mid-flight creates retraining burden.
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jun 9, 2026

decisions.text: The course offering landing page in phase 1 is limited to information that currently exists in the system — no future-state data. Performance analytics, accommodations, and interventions are explicitly excluded from the initial build and will be introduced incrementally as those features are built in later phases. The design must not anticipate data that does not yet exist.
decisions.source: Exam Management Sync up transcript — Jun 9, 2026

decisions.text: Focus on selling this module independently in Q2, 2027. PCE/CE module will be positioned as a standalone commercial offering, separate from the core Prism suite.
decisions.source: PCE PRD §2 Key Product Decisions #6

decisions.text: No Student login for the PCE/CE module until Q3, 2027. Students access course evaluations via email link only (email-only distribution as per pce-decision-021). No student portal authentication for CE in phase 1 or phase 2.
decisions.source: PCE PRD §2 Key Product Decisions #7

decisions.text: Directory tabs (Term, Course, Faculty, Student) must include contextual entry points into the Create Survey wizard. When a user selects one or more courses from the Course directory, a 'Push survey' action is surfaced — opening the Create Survey wizard pre-scoped to the selected courses and landing at Step 2 (Scope/Courses already populated). Similar contextual push-survey entry points apply from the other directory tabs. This is the primary survey-creation path from within each directory tab.
decisions.source: Exam management and course evaluation design with Monil transcript — Jun 16, 2026

decisions.text: The analytics views (by term, by faculty, by course) are dual-homed: they exist as dedicated entries in the Analytics sidebar section AND are accessible from within their respective directory tabs. When a user navigates to a specific course, faculty member, or term in the directory, they can access that item's evaluation analytics inline without navigating to the Analytics sidebar section. Aarti whiteboarded this explicitly during the India office visit; Monil confirmed it as a firm requirement — 'This same view she wants inside respective tabs also.'
decisions.source: Exam management and course evaluation design with Monil transcript — Jun 16, 2026

decisions.text: Course type (Optional) taxonomy updated to three categories: Practice, Classroom, Lab — replacing the original Didactic/Clinical two-category system from pce-decision-008. All three course types are optional when creating a template. The PRD §2 Key Product Decisions #5 now reads 'Practice / Classroom / Lab' as the enumerated options.
decisions.source: PCE PRD §2 Key Product Decisions #5 (updated)

decisions.text: Remove 'send evaluation' (or 'push survey') CTA from current term and last term dashboard cards. Those cards only support 'view term' and alert-based CTAs (e.g., 'send reminders now', 'add missing info'). The send/push CTA is not actionable on an already-running or completed term.
decisions.source: Dashboard and analytics design — messaging, KPIs, and multi-survey structure transcript — Jul 13, 2026

decisions.text: Rename all label instances of 'send evaluation' to 'setup evaluations' throughout the PCE dashboard and wizard. The action is not sending (that implies delivery) — it is configuring/setting up evaluations for a term. Yash flagged this terminology issue during review.
decisions.source: Dashboard and analytics design — messaging, KPIs, and multi-survey structure transcript — Jul 13, 2026

decisions.text: Upcoming term card: replace 'view term' CTA with 'setup survey' (or 'setup evaluations'). Clicking this CTA opens the setup survey wizard with term and academic year pre-filled from the card context. The 'view term' CTA does not apply to upcoming terms because there is no evaluation data yet to view.
decisions.source: Dashboard and analytics design — messaging, KPIs, and multi-survey structure transcript — Jul 13, 2026

decisions.text: The setup survey wizard starts directly from the 'course readiness' step — it does not include 'term details' as step 1. Term calendar configuration (academic year, term start/end dates) is a separate standalone process ('configure a term calendar'), not a step inside the setup survey wizard. When users click 'setup survey' from a term card, term context is already pre-filled.
decisions.source: Dashboard and analytics design — messaging, KPIs, and multi-survey structure transcript — Jul 13, 2026

decisions.text: Faculty column in the dashboard term table: show faculty count (e.g., '2') instead of full names, with a tooltip on hover showing the names. If profile images are mandated and available, 2 stacked avatars may be shown instead. Long faculty names would overflow the column width, so count + tooltip is the correct pattern.
decisions.source: Dashboard and analytics design — messaging, KPIs, and multi-survey structure transcript — Jul 13, 2026

decisions.text: Students column in the dashboard term table: omit it. The number of students a survey is going to is already communicated through per-row response stats (e.g., '4 out of 60'). A redundant students column adds clutter without new information.
decisions.source: Dashboard and analytics design — messaging, KPIs, and multi-survey structure transcript — Jul 13, 2026

decisions.text: Rename 'opens' label on the upcoming term card KPI to 'term starts' (not 'survey opens'). The PCE dashboard must always disambiguate between term start/end dates and survey start/end dates — never use 'start' or 'end' without qualifying which date type it refers to.
decisions.source: Dashboard and analytics design — messaging, KPIs, and multi-survey structure transcript — Jul 13, 2026

decisions.text: Single survey analytics (view results for an individual course-offering survey — the 'view results' page accessible from the dashboard) must be handed to engineering by end of week Jul 13, 2026. Multi-survey analytics (the Analytics tab — by term, by faculty, by course longitudinal views) does NOT need to be frozen this week.
decisions.source: Dashboard and analytics design — messaging, KPIs, and multi-survey structure transcript — Jul 13, 2026

decisions.text: PCE Analytics tab structure — each sub-tab (by term, by faculty, by course) follows exactly 3 layers: (1) Top-level KPIs, (2) Trend graphs (longitudinal view across all terms — collapses to a single data point when the user filters to one specific term), (3) Deep-dive table or navigation (actionable breakdown for the selected single term/faculty/course). Clicking a data point in the trend graph should filter the view to that entity. Do not share the analytics prototype URL with the AI agent — use it as a reference only to avoid biased solutions.
decisions.source: Dashboard and analytics design — messaging, KPIs, and multi-survey structure transcript — Jul 13, 2026

decisions.text: By-faculty analytics is the highest-priority sub-tab. It contains: (a) a leaderboard table of all faculty sorted by score (the program director's primary view), (b) clicking a faculty member opens a single-faculty detail view showing multi-survey longitudinal performance by term and by course, (c) clicking a course card in the faculty detail view navigates to that course-offering's single-survey analytics (the final data node). This drills from leaderboard → faculty → single survey result.
decisions.source: Dashboard and analytics design — messaging, KPIs, and multi-survey structure transcript — Jul 13, 2026

decisions.text: PCE analytics reporting is the final module leg: all on-screen analytics views must eventually support user-selectable filters and export to Excel or PDF. Whatever is shown on screen — faculty leaderboard, course scores, term trends — users can filter and produce a report. This is not phase 1 scope but must be designed with the reporting leg in mind.
decisions.source: Dashboard and analytics design — messaging, KPIs, and multi-survey structure transcript — Jul 13, 2026

decisions.text: PCE Settings/Setup section is deprioritized for design in phase 1 — most settings features are deferred to phase 2. Design attention should focus on Dashboard, Templates, Create Survey (push), View Survey/Results, and Analytics before Settings.
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Jul 9, 2026

decisions.text: PCE dashboard and all PCE admin tables must use the full available horizontal screen width where content density warrants it. Tables rendering at ~70% width when there is available space to use 100% are a layout defect. Overflow should scroll horizontally within the table container, not within the page body. Wide data tables (course list, term table) should use available space rather than forcing scroll where space exists.
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Jul 9, 2026

decisions.text: Accommodations feature is explicitly NOT in Exam Management phase 1 scope — do not design it. No point building any UI for accommodations in the first phase. Phase 1 scope is limited to: Question Creation (P0), Assessment Creation, In-Assessment Experience, Course Offering, and Base Entities.
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Jul 7, 2026

decisions.text: Question creation is Romit's P0 for Exam Management design work — the next priority after PCE view survey is completed. Assessment creation already has working product team prototypes; design refinement is the task (not a rebuild from scratch). Question creation needs to be designed completely from scratch — there are no product team prototypes for it.
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Jul 7, 2026

decisions.text: Yash is the new leadership sponsor for design approvals on both Exam Management and PCE. Aarti reviews approximately once every 1.5 months — she is not a frequent day-to-day reviewer. The PM team (Monil for PCE, Nipun/Bhargav for Exam Management) are day-to-day reviewers, with Yash as final approver. Weekly call with Aarti is canceled indefinitely. This replaces the prior structure where Aarti and Vishaka were frequent stakeholder reviewers.
decisions.source: 1:1 meeting with Arun and Romit transcript — Jul 6, 2026; Course Eval sync up transcript — Jul 7, 2026

decisions.text: Design priority order: Exam Management is #1, PCE/Course Evaluation is #2. When forced to choose between the two and there is an active Exam Management need, prioritize Exam Management. Both products must be the exclusive focus — no other work.
decisions.source: 1:1 meeting with Arun and Romit transcript — Jul 6, 2026

decisions.text: The 'Settings' tab throughout the PCE/CE module must be renamed to 'Setup' to align with Prism product convention. All other areas of Prism use 'setup' not 'settings'. This applies to the sidebar label, page headings, and any CTAs referring to the configuration section. Vishaka: 'In rest of the Prism product, I think we are using the term setup. If I'm not wrong. So any particular reason why we are changing it to settings in this particular module? It is setup. So maybe, Monil, we want to stick to that and not create new terms. So maybe setup is what we want to use.'
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jul 14, 2026

decisions.text: PCE survey takers are limited to students only in phase 1. Contributing faculty (faculty who contribute to a team-taught course) and staff are explicitly out of scope as survey takers. If contributing faculty feedback on course performance is required, it will be addressed in a future phase. Monil: 'No, this is only students. For now. The scope is only students.' Vishaka confirmed: 'if contributing faculty also, we want to collect feedback on the course performance, we are not going to cater to that in phase 1.' This is a good future requirement to capture but not in scope now.
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jul 14, 2026

decisions.text: The CE module landing page (reached after clicking the CE tile from the Prism main menu) must be a unified 'home page' overview rather than defaulting directly to either the CE Dashboard or the Programmatic Survey Dashboard. The home page shows both CE and programmatic surveys at a glance (e.g., active survey counts, response stats for both types) and provides navigation paths to each. Monil: 'Let us think of a home page kind of a thing before we land on this.' Vishaka and David agreed: 'Yeah, that will be better — either it gives them an overview and a couple of ways to go about it, or give them a nice total of what they have active.' Exact design TBD but the direction is confirmed.
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jul 14, 2026

decisions.text: The PCE CE dashboard must be designed for 4 distinct fill states: (1) Empty state — no term configured yet; show a single card that says 'no upcoming term — configure term calendar.' (2) Current term only — first term is set up and live; no last term or upcoming term card. (3) Current + last term — two cards visible; no upcoming term. (4) All three cards — current, last, and upcoming term visible. Monil: 'We need to also capture all these scenarios. One scenario is where the user comes for the first time, which is the empty state. Where nothing is configured. Then one scenario where current term, the first term is set up and it is live. There is neither the last term nor the upcoming term. Another scenario is where you have one last term and one current term and no future term. And the fourth scenario you have all the terms. Right now we have only captured the fourth scenario.'
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jul 14, 2026

decisions.text: PCE beta launch target: build-ready by September 15, 2026 (aligned with the cohere 2026 conference). Beta users are programs that sign up at or before the conference. Only beta-enrolled programs will see the CE tile in Prism — it will not be visible to all users until GA. Beta signups collected via a QR code at the product booth and at the end of the PCE/Exam Management session slide decks (one common QR code covers all new modules). The QR code links to a sign-up form that lets programs express interest in PCE, Exam Management, and Accreditation. Beta usage is free. The goal during the Q4 beta period is to hand-hold 5–10 programs through Prism data setup so they are ready to distribute CE for fall 2026 end-of-term evaluations.
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jul 14, 2026

decisions.text: PCE general announcement (GA) is targeted for January (first or second Friday — exact date TBD). At GA, all Prism users will see the CE tile and the module will be publicly available. Monetization model: free-tier of approximately 6 months from sign-up date, followed by automatic payment. Payment details must be collected at sign-up (prior to the end of the free period) to enable automatic billing — not after the free period ends. Pricing tiers and GTM strategy (product-led vs. AM-assisted) are still being finalized with marketing and sales. Current programmatic survey users who have been using surveys for free will need contract updates from account managers before GA. Monil proposed: 'For beta users, it is going to be free. For GA users we should collect payment details upfront so automatic billing kicks in.' All parties agreed this is the right model to avoid the retroactive payment problem.
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jul 14, 2026

decisions.text: Clinical term edge case (PA programs): Some PA programs configure a year-long 'clinical term' or 'clinical phase' that spans the entire academic year (e.g., July 2026–June 2027). Because CE distribution is anchored to term start/end dates, a clinical term with year-long dates will always appear as a 'current term' on the CE dashboard. This edge case cannot be ignored and must be investigated and designed for before the dashboard is finalized. Action: David to ask Carol (a PA client, Shenandoah) how they currently collect course evaluations for clinical courses — whether per rotation block or at the end of the clinical year. Monil: 'Depending now that if you collect the start date and end date of the clinical term, they will likely put it as July 2026 to June 2027, which is their clinical year. Then it will always show up as a current term on your dashboard.'
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jul 14, 2026

decisions.text: Action needed column in the course readiness table: all faculty-role-specific add CTAs (e.g., 'add instructor', 'add lab instructor', 'add course coordinator') must be aggregated into a single 'add faculty' CTA. If student roster is empty (count = 0), an 'add students' CTA is shown. Maximum two CTAs visible per row at any time: 'add faculty' and/or 'add students'. No per-role CTAs as separate buttons — this would not scale to programs with 5+ faculty roles. Vishal: 'We can categorize all the faculty roles as add faculty CTA. And all the students as add student. So there is only maximum two CTAs that you will see.' The admin knows which roles to add because they are familiar with their program's role configuration.
decisions.source: Course evaluation setup — design feedback and UX refinement transcript — Jul 14, 2026

decisions.text: Cohort and 'what to evaluate' selectors in the setup survey wizard must not use horizontal radio buttons. Cohort is a program-level lookup from Prism (NOT dependent on term or academic year — it is a standalone configuration value) and can have more than 20 values. 'What to evaluate' faculty roles can have 45–50 options per program. Both fields need a scalable UI pattern (e.g., dropdown, searchable multi-select, or tag picker) that handles large option sets without overflowing horizontal space. Vishal: 'Cohort can be more than five... cohort is not dependent on terminal academic year. It is just a defined lookup value that comes from Prism.' And: 'What to evaluate, there are 45, 50 faculty roles created in the system.'
decisions.source: Course evaluation setup — design feedback and UX refinement transcript — Jul 14, 2026

decisions.text: Step 1 of the setup survey wizard ('course readiness') has a single primary purpose: to audit course data and help the admin identify and prepare missing data before distribution — NOT primarily to select which courses to evaluate (courses are already known by the admin). The step surfaces where faculty roles, student rosters, or course offering data are missing so the admin can navigate to Prism, fix the gaps, and return. Labels and language on this step must communicate the audit/preparation intent. Vishal: 'The purpose of step 1 is to audit the course data and help user prepare that data. Preparation will happen in Prism. But what best we can do is we can just identify where are the missing data points. And they can go and fill and come back.' If only the language/copy needs to change (not the structure), a copy change may be sufficient before a full UX rethink.
decisions.source: Course evaluation setup — design feedback and UX refinement transcript — Jul 14, 2026

decisions.text: Dashboard term cards must show a 'create template' CTA in states where no template has yet been created — specifically for upcoming terms or programs setting up their first evaluation. This CTA appears alongside 'setup evaluations'. It does NOT appear for programs or terms where a prior survey has already been pushed (a template already exists for those).
decisions.source: Vishal PM sync transcript — Jul 20, 2026

decisions.text: Setup survey wizard is finalized as 4 steps: (1) Course selection + zero-student identification; (2) Template assignment per course + evaluity (what to evaluate) derived from template + duplicate soft warning; (3) Communication (email, reminders, dates); (4) Review and consent for any warnings. The 'what to evaluate' field is removed from step 1 — it is now derived automatically from the template selected in step 2. Step 1 is course readiness only.
decisions.source: Survey evaluation workflow — step separation and duplicate detection transcript — Jul 24, 2026

decisions.text: A duplicate evaluation is defined as the combination of (course offering ID + faculty role type + person ID). A soft warning is shown in step 2 of the setup wizard when this exact triple already has a live survey. It is NOT a hard block — the admin can proceed. This rule may be hardened to a block later if data supports it.
decisions.source: Survey evaluation workflow — step separation and duplicate detection transcript — Jul 24, 2026

decisions.text: Template creation step order is restored to: (1) Template settings (name, course type, and metadata) FIRST; (2) Template builder (FaaS UI with sections and questions) SECOND. This reverses any prior exploration of putting the builder before settings.
decisions.source: PCE template creation — step order and analytics filter hierarchy transcript — Jul 22, 2026

decisions.text: Single-survey analytics faculty filter follows a two-level hierarchy: faculty role type first, then person within that role. Example: selecting 'Instructor' as the role shows Dr. John and Dr. David; selecting 'Coordinator' shows Dr. Maya. The filter is not a flat list of all faculty.
decisions.source: PCE template creation — step order and analytics filter hierarchy transcript — Jul 22, 2026

decisions.text: One template = one survey is the confirmed publishing architecture. Multiple templates per survey are not supported. Trade-off accepted: template creation may be more complex (each template fully specifies one survey), but publishing is simple — the admin makes one template selection per course with no further multi-template choices. Vishal: 'One template means one survey. So if we have multiple templates, then template creation might be complex. But while publishing a survey, the user will not have multiple selections to do.'
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Jul 21, 2026

decisions.text: Exam download capability is removed from the MVP (Jan 20 launch). Students take exams online with a password for the Jan launch. Download functionality is targeted for limited availability in March. SUPERSEDES exam-decision-001.
decisions.source: Exam management weekly call transcript — Jul 23, 2026

decisions.text: Faculty must be able to manually adjust scores at two levels in the grade review screen before LMS push: (1) question level — remove a question from scoring entirely or award bonus points to everyone; (2) individual student level — override a specific student's score. Both adjustment types are required.
decisions.source: Exam management weekly call transcript — Jul 23, 2026

decisions.text: Point-by-serial (PBS) is calculated at the per-assessment level (specific class + assessment instance) as the primary metric. Historical PBS across all uses of the same assessment is secondary context. Both the per-assessment PBS and the historical PBS should be available in the analytics view.
decisions.source: Exam management weekly call transcript — Jul 23, 2026

decisions.text: Cronbach's alpha is to be researched as a potential assessment-level quality metric (internal consistency measure), in parity with ExamSoft. This is a research action item — Aarti directed Vishal and Nipun to investigate it before it becomes a design decision.
decisions.source: Exam management weekly call transcript — Jul 23, 2026

decisions.text: Student-initiated evaluations are NOT in scope for phase 1 of PCE. All evaluations are triggered by the admin for a specific admin-defined window. Guest lecturer feedback can be configured by the admin for a custom window independent of term dates, but the initiation mechanism remains admin-triggered (not student-triggered). The student-initiated evaluation mechanism (as implemented in Exxat Lamp/Evaluations module) is not being replicated in the PCE module for phase 1. Monil: 'Right now we will not support student initiated evaluations. All of them are triggered by admin for a specific window.'
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jul 28, 2026

decisions.text: DCE (Director of Clinical Education) 360 evaluation is general survey scope — not course evaluation scope. It is a once-a-year institution-wide survey where students evaluate the DCE's management of clinical education program-wide. It is not tied to a specific course or term, so it does not qualify as a course evaluation. Programs that want to collect post-course feedback on individual clinical courses may still do so via the CE module with custom windows.
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jul 28, 2026

decisions.text: 'Mark as default for course type' toggle is removed from the template creation step. If a default-template mechanism is needed, it must live on the template list page (where all templates are listed) — not inside template creation. Both Vishaka and David found the toggle confusing inside template creation. Vishaka: 'So this might confuse or complicate or they might not understand what this bit is going to do for them' and 'remove it completely.'
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jul 28, 2026

decisions.text: Course type selector in template creation is multi-select (not single-select). A single template can apply to multiple course types simultaneously — a nursing program may have a single course with classroom, lab, and experiential components. The single-select UI prevents this valid use case. Multi-select allows the template to cover all applicable course type components in one template.
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jul 28, 2026

decisions.text: Faculty role sections in the template builder are single-select per tab (one role configured at a time). When the user adds a second faculty role, the system must offer to clone/copy questions from the previously configured role so the user can then edit/tweak. Multi-selecting all roles at once is removed — it implies shared questions but masks the typical need for role-specific questions. Vishaka: 'Just give them the ability to curate questions for one role at a time. And if they pick, choose additional roles, you give them the option to copy the same question from the previous role.'
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jul 28, 2026

decisions.text: 'Practice' course type is renamed to 'Experiential' to better represent rotation/clinical experiential courses. The three course types are now: Classroom, Lab, Experiential — replacing the previous Classroom, Lab, Practice taxonomy from pce-decision-040. Monil: 'Let's note it down and change it to experiential.' The term 'Experiential' better aligns with pharmacy and health professions vocabulary for placement-based and rotation-based courses.
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jul 28, 2026

decisions.text: Template builder navigation: clicking 'next' in any template section must advance the user through ALL sections in sequence — including faculty sections — without requiring manual panel navigation. If a 'next' button exists, users expect it to guide the full journey. The left-panel section list should reflect progress/completion state, but the primary navigation is sequential via 'next'. Vishaka: 'I didn't realize I had to go on the left hand panel, click faculty and complete that. Because if I see a next button, I'm gonna that you're going to take me through the whole journey.'
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jul 28, 2026

decisions.text: PCE analytics: faculty of the same role type must be compared against each other — course coordinators compared with course coordinators, instructors with instructors, lab assistants with lab assistants. Cross-role comparisons are not the baseline analytics pattern. David: 'Course coordinator should be compared with course coordinators. Instructors should be compared with instructors.' Monil confirmed: 'Correct.'
decisions.source: Post-Course Survey Cadence Meeting (BiWeely 45 Mins) transcript — Jul 28, 2026

decisions.text: Email templates, reminder templates, and reminder frequency are CENTRAL settings — not per-survey-distribution settings. They are configured once in the Setup section and auto-fetched when the admin reaches step 3 (Communication) of the setup survey wizard. There is no per-survey communication customization in phase 1. Monil: 'We will have email templates, reminder templates and reminder frequency as Central settings. Which will not be per survey distribution. It is a setting that is saved and whatever is saved will be fetched. When we jump on step three.'
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Jul 28, 2026

decisions.text: The course readiness table in the setup survey flow must surface three distinct course states: (1) Not yet configured — action CTA: 'Setup'; (2) In progress — partially configured, saved draft, editable; (3) Fully configured / scheduled for distribution — editable (add/remove faculty, change communication dates) before the distribution date passes; after distribution date, becomes read-only/locked. These three states drive distinct available actions per row and prevent inadvertent duplicate setups. David: 'I almost see three cases, right? So here, nothing has been set up for this course and this time frame. It's in progress... Or the third, they've configured it all the way through. They've sent it and scheduled it for distribution.'
decisions.source: Exact Prism evaluation setup — UX feedback and workflow refinement transcript — Jul 31, 2026

decisions.text: Bulk multi-select of courses in the setup survey flow is restricted to courses in 'Not yet configured' state. Courses that are already configured (states 2 or 3) cannot be bulk-selected alongside unconfigured courses — they require individual editing. This prevents mixing new-setup and edit-existing workflows in a single batch action. David: 'You wouldn't allow them to multiple select. You can multiple select courses you haven't configured at all yet. But as soon as I've configured a course, I shouldn't be able to select that and select a course I haven't configured.'
decisions.source: Exact Prism evaluation setup — UX feedback and workflow refinement transcript — Jul 31, 2026

decisions.text: In the setup survey wizard step 2 (template assignment), the template name must be shown — not the course name — as the primary label for each evaluation section. Displaying the course name when the user is assigning a template creates confusion: the user already selected the course in step 1. Showing course names implies they are picking courses again, not templates. David: 'the fact that you're listing course names when my brain is thinking I'm picking a template is really confusing me.'
decisions.source: Exact Prism evaluation setup — UX feedback and workflow refinement transcript — Jul 31, 2026

decisions.text: After an evaluation's distribution date passes (the evaluation is live and sent to students), it is locked — no further changes are permitted. Before the distribution date: adding/removing faculty and editing communication dates is allowed. This prevents creating inconsistent response sets where some students answer one version of the evaluation and others answer a different version after faculty were added. David: 'Once the evaluation is sent out, it should lock in my opinion at least. You should not be able to go in and then add other people because then what are you going to get? You're going to get some responses for one version of it and other responses for a different version of it.'
decisions.source: Exact Prism evaluation setup — UX feedback and workflow refinement transcript — Jul 31, 2026

decisions.text: The PCE dashboard must include a direct visible CTA to create or access survey templates — not just accessible through the Settings/Setup sidebar entry. A link or button (e.g., 'Create template' or 'Manage templates') must appear on the dashboard itself, especially in states where no templates exist yet. First-time users land on the dashboard and need to create a template before doing anything else. David: 'I think there needs to be something on the dashboard, especially if there is no templates in their system.'
decisions.source: Exact Prism evaluation setup — UX feedback and workflow refinement transcript — Jul 31, 2026

decisions.text: The 'open surveys / reminders' informational overview (showing all active surveys in the current term) must be removed from the communication step of the setup survey wizard. It creates a dead stop — users wonder what action is needed but none is required. This overview belongs on the dashboard, not inside a per-survey setup flow. David: 'I might think about if we need this or not because as a user like I'm stopping here and being like, what do I need to do with this? If it's just like an fyi, I don't know if we need to surface in the workflow because right now I'm planning the communication for this particular course.'
decisions.source: Exact Prism evaluation setup — UX feedback and workflow refinement transcript — Jul 31, 2026

decisions.text: Assessment creation supports two primary user journeys, and AI assists in both: (1) Repurpose existing assessment — the most common case; faculty import a full past assessment and tweak it (adjust for schedule changes, increase rigor, swap topics). AI helps identify gaps or improve the imported set. (2) Create from scratch — faculty build a new assessment by picking from the question bank or having AI generate questions based on a described scope. Both paths converge at the same review and publish steps. Starting from scratch is the rare case; most faculty already have prior assessments to build from.
decisions.source: Exam management weekly call transcript — Jul 30, 2026

decisions.text: Assessment repurposing (import path) uses full-assessment import — one complete assessment at a time. The interface imports all questions from the selected assessment as the starting point. Pick-and-choose across multiple assessments question-by-question is NOT the repurpose use case; that belongs in the question bank selection flow. Multiple sequential full-assessment imports are supported (e.g., import 50 questions from midterm 1, then import 20 more from midterm 2), but done as separate import actions — not as multi-select from a split view.
decisions.source: Exam management weekly call transcript — Jul 30, 2026

decisions.text: Cross-course question access in assessment creation is governed by faculty course association only — no topic-based or same-subject restrictions. Faculty can import assessments from any course they are associated with, regardless of whether subjects overlap. The system must not assume or enforce topic boundaries. Aarti: 'We as a technology platform should not limit them... we can limit them based on their access. So if they're associated with the courses they can pull from assessments of those courses. But we should not build any constraints or restrictions based on the topic.'
decisions.source: Exam management weekly call transcript — Jul 30, 2026

decisions.text: The PBS (point-by-serial) threshold that triggers a question-quality flag in the assessment builder is admin-configurable. The institution admin sets the threshold (e.g., PBS ≤ 0) in settings. Questions below the threshold are flagged with a visual indicator during assessment creation, prompting faculty to make a deliberate choice to retain them. Aarti confirmed: 'I like the idea to make that threshold customizable wherein if the school says that any question that has a point by serial of zero or less, we want to bring that in our radar. Then I think that's a good feature to have.'
decisions.source: Exam management weekly call transcript — Jul 30, 2026

decisions.text: AI in assessment creation should surface and bubble up the most relevant questions from the question bank based on the assessment scope (e.g., lecture range, course objectives) — but must NOT restrict or block faculty from picking questions from other courses or folders. AI assistance is suggestive, not prescriptive. Aarti: 'AI will help them bring before them or bubble up the most relevant information based on what they provide us... but not limit or restrict if they still want to pick questions from another course folder we are not going to stop them from doing that right.'
decisions.source: Exam management weekly call transcript — Jul 30, 2026

decisions.text: Step 2 of the setup survey wizard must visually distinguish non-person aspects (course content, general) from person-based aspects (all faculty roles). Non-person aspects require no further person-assignment action. Person-based aspects require identifying which specific individuals fill that role and must prompt the admin to assign or confirm faculty in Prism. Vishal: 'I would force you to also think from a human and non-human aspect separately so that the next information where user needs to take action can also be intuitively filled.'
decisions.source: Step two design — template selection, aspect deduplication, and auto-update logic with Romit transcript — Aug 4, 2026

decisions.text: The same aspect (e.g., course content, instructor role) cannot be evaluated twice for the same course offering in the same term — this is a hard block, not a soft warning. If a scheduled or live survey already evaluates 'course content' for a given course offering, any new survey for that same course cannot include 'course content'. The duplicate is detected using (course offering ID + aspect being evaluated). The blocked aspect is deselected and shown with a hard-block indicator; the admin can proceed only with non-duplicated aspects. Vishal: 'We will not allow admins to create same survey for course and aspect combination.' and 'Hard block. Why? Because you have already evaluated course [content]... you will not allow this.'
decisions.source: Step two design — template selection, aspect deduplication, and auto-update logic with Romit transcript — Aug 4, 2026

decisions.text: When an admin selects a course in step 2 that already has a scheduled survey and switches to a different template, the system must present two explicit paths: (a) Override — completely replaces the existing scheduled survey with the new template; the old survey is deleted and the new one takes its place. (b) Create new survey — a separate survey coexists alongside the existing one; any aspect already evaluated in the existing survey is hard-blocked (pce-decision-086) in the new survey. The system must surface this choice to the admin at the moment of template switch, as the two paths have very different consequences. Vishal: 'There can be two scenarios: you want to override or create a new survey... Override: you only have one entry. The survey that was in scheduled is now this survey scheduled... Creating new survey is this: two surveys both exist in the system.'
decisions.source: Step two design — template selection, aspect deduplication, and auto-update logic with Romit transcript — Aug 4, 2026

decisions.text: Auto update toggle behavior in step 2: Auto update ON means whatever faculty are associated with the course in Prism at the moment the survey goes live (not at setup time) are automatically included. If a new instructor is added to Prism between setup and go-live, they are automatically pulled into the evaluation. Auto update OFF means only faculty explicitly assigned at setup time are included; any Prism additions made after setup are ignored. When auto update is OFF, the UI must show any Prism faculty who exist for the course but are excluded (shown in a deselected/disabled state) so the admin knows they are missing from the evaluation. Vishal: 'If the auto update toggle was on... whatever are the person in Prism... John will also be part of this course evaluation... if auto update was off... whatever was defined on day one... John will not be added even if John is present in Prism... you will have to show [this] so that user knows... there is another person called John but is not being evaluated.'
decisions.source: Step two design — template selection, aspect deduplication, and auto-update logic with Romit transcript — Aug 4, 2026

decisions.text: A manual refresh button must be present in step 2 of the setup survey wizard to pull the latest faculty associations from Prism on demand. When clicked, refresh pulls updated faculty data from Prism and updates the evaluity column for all courses shown — adding newly assigned faculty and removing any removed ones. This is distinct from the auto update toggle (pce-decision-088): refresh is a one-time manual pull; auto update is an ongoing automatic sync up to go-live. Vishal: 'Right now you can propose a manual refresh button on the top... Refresh is getting all the data from Prism... pulling all the latest faculty associations to Prism to this module.'
decisions.source: Step two design — template selection, aspect deduplication, and auto-update logic with Romit transcript — Aug 4, 2026

decisions.text: The on/off toggle for evaluity selection in step 2 of the setup survey wizard operates at the faculty ROLE level, not at the individual person level. The admin toggles 'Course Material' on or off and 'Instructor' on or off — not per-person (not per Dr. David or Dr. John). If the role is toggled on, all persons assigned to that role are included. The count or names of persons within the role can be shown as a summary alongside the role toggle, but the toggle itself controls the role, not individual persons. Monil: 'This toggle would be only on the role level... you tell the system that I only want to evaluate course material and instructor... We will not show who the instructors are at this level. We can just give a summary where you have on the top or else we can say show number of instructor personas... But that toggle is not on a person. That toggle is on a role.'
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Aug 6, 2026

decisions.text: Step 2 of the setup survey wizard must be designed for the 80% common case: evaluating only Course Material and Instructor. These two are the default evaluity display. Additional faculty roles (3rd, 4th, 5th, etc.) must be accessible via progressive disclosure — a '+' button, 'See more', or 'View more' pattern. This prevents cognitive overload for the majority of users while still supporting programs with 10+ faculty roles. The design philosophy is: optimize the primary experience for 80% of users; don't penalize them with a complex layout designed for the 20% edge case. Monil: '80% of our users will run course evaluation to evaluate the following: Course material and instructor... Design for those 80%. But our system supports other N faculty roles also. Tomorrow you can evaluate 10 faculty roles... It is like a plus button or see more or view more kind of a thing.'
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Aug 6, 2026

decisions.text: When an admin changes the template selection for a course in step 2, a confirmation dialog must be shown before the change is applied. The dialog must communicate that changing the template will update all evaluities (aspects to be evaluated) based on the new template. The admin must actively confirm the change — template switches are never silent or automatic. Monil: 'You will give a dialogue that are you sure you want to change the template if the template is updated, all the evaluities will also be updated based on the new template selected.'
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Aug 6, 2026

decisions.text: Faculty members must be displayed by name (text only) in the step 2 setup survey wizard and related CE setup screens — not by profile photo or avatar. Rationale: (1) many faculty do not have profile images uploaded in the system; (2) rendering profile images via API adds latency to an already complex page. A/B testing a names-only variant alongside an image variant is acceptable, but names-only is the preferred direction. Monil: 'Let's avoid using images because some of the faculties might not have images uploaded. And rendering image from engineering standpoint is... time consuming. The API calls will take some time to show that image. Instead of that, can we just simply show that instructor in front of instructor you have names of those faculties. You can do A/B testing... we would prefer that over this.'
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Aug 6, 2026

decisions.text: Admins cannot cancel an evaluation from within step 2 of the setup survey wizard. If an admin wants to cancel an evaluation, they must navigate to the View Survey List and cancel from there. No cancel action is exposed in the step 2 UI. Monil: 'They can cancel but not here in this step. They have to go to view survey list and there they can cancel.'
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Aug 6, 2026

decisions.text: When faculty are added to Prism and synced into the CE setup, updated faculty data must appear inline within the evaluity column of the relevant course row in step 2 — not as separate floating cards or a dedicated section above the table. Separate cards create confusion because each instructor is specifically associated with one course; detaching them from the course row breaks that association. For large-scale syncs (e.g., 10 courses each gaining new faculty), the inline approach is essential to keep faculty-course relationships clear. Monil: 'Cards showing separately will confuse the user because each instructor is associated to a course. So it has to be in front of a course line... We can shift things on the left and show newly added evaluities on that evaluity column itself.'
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Aug 6, 2026

decisions.text: No aspect-level or faculty-level template assignment is supported. One template per course per survey push — not multiple templates for different aspects or faculty within the same course. Supporting multi-template assignment per course is explicitly not in scope now or in the foreseeable future. The design must not accommodate or hint at per-aspect template selection.
decisions.source: Survey design and review — aspects, templates, and response rates transcript — Aug 12, 2026

decisions.text: Response rate is always calculated and displayed at the survey level, not the aspect level. 80% of use cases involve a single survey per course covering all aspects; 20% may use separate surveys per aspect. The design must optimize for the 80% case — one survey, one response rate per course — while not breaking for the 20% edge case. Aspect-level response rate tracking is out of scope.
decisions.source: Survey design and review — aspects, templates, and response rates transcript — Aug 12, 2026

decisions.text: Step 3 of the setup survey wizard gains two new fields: (1) Survey title — supports merge field placeholders such as {course name}, {academic year}, {term}; the system pre-populates a default title using these placeholders and the admin can edit it. (2) Survey instructions — plain English text displayed to the student at the top of the survey form. Both fields are added to the step 3 distribution configuration screen.
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Aug 11, 2026

decisions.text: Step 3 of the setup survey wizard supports per-course evaluation window overrides. The admin sets a global open date and close date for the survey push; individual courses can have independent date overrides that deviate from the global window. Both the global dates and per-course override capability must be present in the step 3 UI.
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Aug 11, 2026

decisions.text: The reminder frequency configuration section is removed from step 3 of the setup survey wizard. It is deprioritized for this release. Reminder frequency remains a central account-level setting per pce-decision-078 and is not surfaced per-survey in the wizard flow.
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Aug 11, 2026

decisions.text: Result release date is removed from the setup survey wizard entirely. Survey results are NOT automatically distributed to faculty when the survey closes. Instead, the admin manually releases results to faculty on a one-by-one basis from the results dashboard after the survey closes. There is no automated result release — it is always a deliberate admin action per course. Monil: 'We will not have result release date in the survey distribution.'
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Aug 11, 2026

decisions.text: Step 4 (review) of the setup survey wizard displays a table of course offerings with the following columns: course name, evaluation window open/close dates, student count, and named evaluity roles (e.g., 'Instructor, Course Coordinator, Course Material' — not a numeric count). The template column is intentionally excluded from the step 4 review table.
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Aug 11, 2026

decisions.text: The Manage Survey screen must support both per-row actions and bulk actions. Per-row actions include: remind (send reminder for one course), extend (extend the window for one course), and edit (edit configuration for one course). Bulk actions include: select multiple courses and send bulk reminders to all selected. Both granularity levels are required — admins must be able to act on individual courses and on groups of courses simultaneously.
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Aug 11, 2026

decisions.text: Two school-configurable response rate thresholds must be supported: (1) a validity floor — the minimum response rate below which a survey result cannot be used for comparative analysis; (2) a desired participation rate — the school's participation target. These define three color zones displayed in the UI: red (below validity floor), orange (above floor but below target), green (at or above target). The system provides recommended default values for both thresholds; schools can override them in settings.
decisions.source: Course evaluation survey — roles, status tracking, and response rate thresholds transcript — Aug 12, 2026

decisions.text: The live-survey view must be architecturally split into two separate pages or tabs with distinct role-based access: (1) Collection dashboard — for setup admins; shows completion counts, send reminders, extend dates, and preview the survey form but never reveals ratings or comments. (2) Results view — for program directors; shows content, ratings, and comments but exposes no logistics actions. The two views are kept separate to enforce clean role-based access and prevent accidental data exposure.
decisions.source: Survey completion dashboard and role-based admin design with Vishal transcript — Aug 12, 2026

decisions.text: Survey date extensions are rare exceptions and must be visually highlighted wherever they appear. Any course whose evaluation window has been individually extended must display a distinct visual indicator (e.g., 'Extended · closes Aug 30') so admins immediately recognize it as a deviation from the standard term-level close date. All surveys are generally expected to close on the same term-level date; extensions are exceptions, not the norm.
decisions.source: Course evaluation survey — roles, status tracking, and response rate thresholds transcript — Aug 12, 2026

decisions.text: The system must provide an archive or deactivate capability for incorrectly configured surveys. Use the terminology 'archive' or 'deactivate' — never 'delete.' This capability is required to handle cases where an admin configured the wrong faculty, wrong course, or wrong template. Archiving removes the survey from active lists without permanently deleting data.
decisions.source: Course evaluation survey — roles, status tracking, and response rate thresholds transcript — Aug 12, 2026

decisions.text: Email template merge fields for the subject line are separate from merge fields for the email body. Some body-level fields (e.g., specific course name) are inappropriate for the subject line when the email is distributed across multiple courses simultaneously. The email template editor UI must allow admins to insert merge fields independently into the subject line and the body — the two merge field sets are not interchangeable.
decisions.source: Survey design and email template configuration for course evaluation transcript — Aug 13, 2026

decisions.text: When a survey contains questions using different Likert scales, those questions must be grouped into separate sections in analytics — never aggregated across different scales. Each scale grouping gets its own dedicated section, its own distribution visualization, and its own average calculation. Mixing different Likert scales in a single aggregate metric is explicitly prohibited.
decisions.source: Survey completion dashboard and role-based admin design with Vishal transcript — Aug 12, 2026

decisions.text: Survey scheduling does not lock in student targets at schedule time. At the moment a survey goes live, the system reads whoever is currently enrolled in the course. Students added after scheduling are automatically included; students removed after scheduling are excluded. There are no pre-created per-student distribution targets at scheduling time.
decisions.source: Course evaluation setup — survey design, scheduling, and notification templates transcript — Aug 17, 2026

decisions.text: Courses that already have a scheduled or live survey must be excluded (unchecked and not pre-selected) by default in setup wizard step 1. Do not default-select already-scheduled courses alongside unconfigured ones — this creates ambiguity about whether the admin is setting up from scratch or overriding an existing survey. Only courses needing action (not yet configured) are pre-selected.
decisions.source: Course evaluation setup — survey design, scheduling, and notification templates transcript — Aug 17, 2026

decisions.text: Default rows-per-page in all CE survey/course tables is 25 (not 10). The bias in every CE screen should be showing more information in a more compact way.
decisions.source: Course evaluation setup — survey design, scheduling, and notification templates transcript — Aug 17, 2026

decisions.text: Per-course date override in the setup wizard uses the verb 'edit' not 'add custom rule.' Each course either uses the default dates or has its dates edited individually — it is a course-by-course date edit, not a named rule applied to groups of courses. A '+' button with the label 'add custom rule' is incorrect.
decisions.source: Course evaluation setup — survey design, scheduling, and notification templates transcript — Aug 17, 2026

decisions.text: The CE email template editor must match the capabilities of the existing Prism notification hub template editor: rich text editing, header and footer with university logo, attachment support, preview button, set-as-default option, and merge fields. The same Prism users who use notification templates will use CE email templates — a lesser experience in CE will create immediate user complaints. Reference the existing Prism template editor as the baseline, then improve on it.
decisions.source: Course evaluation setup — survey design, scheduling, and notification templates transcript — Aug 17, 2026

decisions.text: The CE email sender address (from: exxat surveys or equivalent) must be customizable per university. The UI must include an instruction that communicates this address can be changed to the university's own address. An edit button or link to configure this should be present, though it can be implemented in a follow-up pass.
decisions.source: Course evaluation setup — survey design, scheduling, and notification templates transcript — Aug 17, 2026

decisions.text: Setup term (configuring which Prism terms are enabled for CE) and setup evaluations (distributing surveys for a term) are fully separate workflows. After setting up a term, the user has two choices: configure more terms, or set up evaluations for that term. The setup evaluation wizard does not embed term configuration as a sub-step.
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Aug 18, 2026

decisions.text: All analytics calculations must happen at the term level — never merge raw data from multiple terms. Cross-term comparisons use average-of-averages: each term's average gets equal weighting regardless of student count. A term with 15 students and a term with 45 students both contribute one equal average to the cross-term aggregate.
decisions.source: Faculty evaluation analytics — term-by-term data structure and dashboard design transcript — Aug 17, 2026

decisions.text: Faculty and course trend charts in analytics must show one data point per term — the final term-level rating. Do not show intra-survey trends (how ratings changed day-by-day during the open survey window). The only meaningful data point is the final rating for the completed term.
decisions.source: Faculty evaluation analytics — term-by-term data structure and dashboard design transcript — Aug 17, 2026

decisions.text: Terms whose response rate falls below the validity floor threshold (pce-decision-104) must be excluded from cross-term average calculations. Below-threshold response rates represent statistically invalid data — including them in cross-term averages would contaminate the aggregate.
decisions.source: Faculty evaluation analytics — term-by-term data structure and dashboard design transcript — Aug 17, 2026

decisions.text: High Charts is the confirmed charting library for all PCE analytics visualizations. All charts must use a consistent High Charts theme across the module.
decisions.source: Faculty evaluation analytics — term-by-term data structure and dashboard design transcript — Aug 17, 2026

decisions.text: Analytics language must use 'best performing' and 'needs attention' — never 'worst performing' for low-rated faculty or courses. The program director views their faculty data; the framing must be constructive and supportive, not punitive or depressing. Show top performers and those 'needing attention,' not top performers and worst performers.
decisions.source: Faculty evaluation analytics — term-by-term data structure and dashboard design transcript — Aug 17, 2026

decisions.text: The by-cohort view in analytics is a separate tab, not a small toggle switch. Cohort-level analytics and term-level analytics are distinct orientations that warrant separate top-level tabs in the analytics structure.
