decisions.source: Faculty evaluation analytics — term-by-term data structure and dashboard design transcript — Aug 17, 2026

decisions.text: When expanding the term-by-term analytics comparison view, show: courses that went up since last term, courses that went down since last term, faculty that went up since last term, faculty that went down since last term. This delta view (needle movers) is more actionable than a full AI narrative summary of all changes.
decisions.source: Faculty evaluation analytics — term-by-term data structure and dashboard design transcript — Aug 17, 2026

decisions.text: Course code must be displayed as a separate column in CE tables (e.g., survey list, manage survey) — not combined or nested under the course name column. Separate columns make it clearer.
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Aug 18, 2026

decisions.text: Multi-select in the manage survey table is restricted to same-status rows only — admins can only bulk-select rows in the same status. Closed and 'results available' rows are non-selectable by default. Actions differ significantly by status, so mixing statuses in a bulk selection is not supported. Bulk actions are available only for: draft, live, and not-configured rows.
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Aug 18, 2026

decisions.text: Board/Kanban view for manage survey is deferred to the second pass. First pass is table view only.
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Aug 18, 2026

decisions.text: Closed and results-available surveys in the manage survey table are surfaced via a collapsed accordion — not in the main table alongside active/draft/live rows. The primary table shows only actionable statuses (not configured, draft, scheduled, live). Closed and published entries are accessible by expanding the accordion.
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Aug 18, 2026

decisions.text: When a user clicks 'setup term' from the CE dashboard empty state, term configuration must open in a drawer on the same page — not navigate the user away to a separate page. After adding a term in the drawer, the user closes the drawer and continues from the dashboard. This prevents breaking the user's workflow.
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Aug 18, 2026

decisions.text: Dashboard KPI language: use 'feedback requests' not 'students' when counting outstanding responses. One student may submit multiple feedback responses (for different faculty roles in the same course), so the count is feedback-level, not student-level. Example: '122 feedback requests still need to respond' is correct; '122 students still need to respond' is incorrect.
decisions.source: Course Eval sync up transcript — Aug 18, 2026

decisions.text: The CE dashboard uses a three-column layout with columns for: Last term (leftmost), Current term (center), Upcoming term (rightmost) — following chronological left-to-right order. This is the confirmed column sequence. Past terms (before last) and future terms (after upcoming) are shown in a separate section below the three cards.
decisions.source: Course evaluation dashboard — term states, card cases, and layout structure with Vishal transcript — Aug 19, 2026

decisions.text: Five term states are defined for the CE dashboard: (1) Current, (2) Upcoming, (3) Last (previous term), (4) Past (any term before Last), (5) Future (any term beyond Upcoming). Only Current, Upcoming, and Last are shown as the three primary columns. Past terms and future terms outside these three are folded into separate sections.
decisions.source: Course evaluation dashboard — term states, card cases, and layout structure with Vishal transcript — Aug 19, 2026

decisions.text: Past terms section in the CE dashboard is shown by default — no 'show more' gate. Past term cards display: academic year, start/end dates, course offerings count, evaluation coverage (percentage as primary text + 'X of Y courses' as subtext), average response rate, program average, course average, faculty average. Actions: view analytics, view survey.
decisions.source: Course evaluation dashboard — term states, card cases, and layout structure with Vishal transcript — Aug 19, 2026

decisions.text: Enabling a term for CE requires that term's start date and end date to be present. Prism terms without start/end dates are ineligible and excluded from CE term setup. The user selects from a list; terms with missing dates are not shown or shown as disabled.
decisions.source: Course evaluation dashboard — term states, card cases, and layout structure with Vishal transcript — Aug 19, 2026

decisions.text: Template configuration is NOT required to show the 'setup evaluations' CTA on a term card. A template is only required when the user reaches step 2 of the setup evaluation wizard — at that point, if no template exists, prompt the user to configure one and provide a navigation link. Do not gate the setup evaluations entry point on template existence.
decisions.source: Course evaluation dashboard — term states, card cases, and layout structure with Vishal transcript — Aug 19, 2026

decisions.text: Evaluation coverage metric on dashboard cards = (count of scheduled + live + closed + published courses) / (total courses in the term). Show the percentage as the primary figure and the raw count as subtext (e.g., '75% · 15 of 20 courses'). Coverage below 100% drives the primary CTA to set up remaining evaluations.
decisions.source: Course evaluation dashboard — term states, card cases, and layout structure with Vishal transcript — Aug 19, 2026

decisions.text: The CE dashboard layout is NOT a Kanban board. It uses a column-based card layout that resembles Kanban visually, but states are system-determined — users cannot drag or move term cards between columns. A true Kanban implies drag-and-drop which would be incorrect here.
decisions.source: Course evaluation dashboard — term states, card cases, and layout structure with Vishal transcript — Aug 19, 2026

decisions.text: Survey status counts on dashboard term cards must show Live count + Scheduled count + total (not 'in review' or vague labels). Example: '30 live · 7 scheduled · 50 total'. Live and Scheduled are the two most actionable statuses and must be explicitly surfaced.
decisions.source: Course evaluation dashboard — term states, card cases, and layout structure with Vishal transcript — Aug 19, 2026

decisions.text: The CE module must be labeled 'Course Surveys' in the UI navigation and product labels — not 'Course Evaluations.' This avoids confusion with 'Evaluations' in Exxat's clinical placement management (Lamp/EXXAT). The word 'survey' better describes the action and is self-explanatory. Aarti confirmed: 'course survey is self-explanatory and it helps us distinguish from evaluations which is a term we use for our clinical placement management.'
decisions.source: Course Eval Design review for Cohere transcript — Aug 20, 2026

decisions.text: Course types for CE templates are confirmed as Didactic and Experiential only. Not Classroom/Lab/Experiential (three types). Aarti: 'didactic and experiential is what we use here as well.' Vishal confirmed: 'we decided to use experiential and didactic.' These two are the only course type taxonomy options.
decisions.source: Course Eval Design review for Cohere transcript — Aug 20, 2026

decisions.text: For the Cohere beta launch, the 'Add template' / self-service template creation capability is hidden from customers. Instead, show an instruction box stating: 'If you want to add a template, please reach out to support@exxat.com with the paper or PDF form of your evaluation form and we will set it up for you.' Engineering may continue developing the capability in the background but it must not be shown to customers until it is production-quality.
decisions.source: Course Eval Design review for Cohere transcript — Aug 20, 2026

decisions.text: The admin management dashboard must not show which specific faculty are rated poorly or well — only program-level aggregate averages (overall program average, overall course average, overall faculty average) are shown on the management-role view. Aarti: 'The only thing that is acceptable to add to the management view is the average rating. Do not show which courses are badly rated and which faculty are badly rated — those become gossip topics for people who don't need visibility into that.' Individual-level ratings belong only in the content/results role view.
decisions.source: Course Eval Design review for Cohere transcript — Aug 20, 2026

decisions.text: Past and future terms must NOT appear as a separate table below the three-column dashboard. Instead, provide a visible action button or link at the top of the dashboard (e.g., 'View all terms' or 'Go to all terms') that navigates to the directory/terms page. This prevents the dashboard from becoming a jumbled multi-section page with too many information layers.
decisions.source: Course evaluations UI — information hierarchy and past/future terms layout transcript — Aug 19, 2026

decisions.text: Programmatic/General surveys are parked for Cohere. Design focus is exclusively on directory and course surveys (CE module) for the Cohere launch. No active design work on programmatic survey flow.
decisions.source: Course evaluations UI — information hierarchy and past/future terms layout transcript — Aug 19, 2026

decisions.text: Design decisions must be backed by real usage data from the deployed Exact product — not hypothetical user behavior. Aarti: 'Today you cannot act as ignorant about the client's real usage as you would have a few years back when you joined. The fact that we are able to pull this information should be baked into how you present your designs to the leadership.' This applies especially to decisions about module-switching frequency, OU code switching, and navigation patterns.
decisions.source: Home page design and login flow — with Aarti transcript — Aug 17, 2026
